title: Cap opening can block risk finalization
detail:
L-01

Cap opening can block risk finalization

Round 1
Sep 6, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/DToken.sol:353-361; source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralVault.sol:253-270
CATEGORY

DoS

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

Reserved branches must finalize their risk parameters before borrowing and Stability Pool deposits become available. AddressesRegistry.finalizeRiskParams requires both the dToken mint cap and total supply to remain zero.

uint256 dTokenCap = dToken.cap();
if (dTokenCap != 0) revert DTokenCapNotZero(dTokenCap);
uint256 dTokenSupply = dToken.totalSupply();
if (dTokenSupply != 0) revert DTokenSupplyNotZero(dTokenSupply);


However, the owner can increase the cap through DToken.setCap without checking whether risk parameters have been finalized. Once the underlying is bound and other deposit requirements are satisfied, CollateralVault.deposit can mint dTokens without checking finalization.

Consequently, if the owner mistakenly opens the cap before risk parameters are finalized, deposits can introduce dToken supply that blocks finalization. Although the owner can restore the cap to zero, finalization will continue reverting until all existing dTokens are burned. A malicious depositor can refuse to redeem or transfer the tokens to an unspendable address, permanently preventing branch activation and forcing a redeployment.

RECOMMENDATION

Consider requiring finalized risk parameters before permitting a nonzero cap or Vault deposits.

title: Written-Off Strategies Can Remain Registered Indefinitely
detail:
L-02

Written-Off Strategies Can Remain Registered Indefinitely

Round 1
Sep 8, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralVault.sol:657-663; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/BaseStrategy.sol:387-396
CATEGORY

OOS - Business logic errors

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

CollateralVault.removeStrategy requires both principal and estimated assets to be readable and zero. However, writeoffStrategyPrincipal only reduces principal. It does not clear tracked shares or change the upstream valuation.

For example, Morpho Vault V1.1 calculates reported assets as realTotalAssets + newLostAssets, adding recorded losses back into its accounting value instead of reducing the share price. An ERC4626Strategy holding its shares can therefore report nonzero assets even if they are unrecoverable due to bad debt.

This also applies to a MorphoV2Strategy whose upstream V2 vault allocates into a V1.1 vault through an adapter that uses the V1.1 share valuation.

Writing off the strategy’s remaining principal still leaves removeStrategy reverting on its nonzero asset estimate. Until the residual position can be cleared, the strategy occupies one of the vault’s 32 strategy slots and remains in every valuation sweep.

RECOMMENDATION

Add an explicit, privileged removal path for fully written-off strategies with unrecoverable positions, allowing deregistration without requiring a zero upstream valuation. Document this path as a final abandonment of the position, to be used only after recovery has been ruled out.

title: Shared Compensation Cap Allows Excessive Liquidator Rewards For dwstETH
detail:
L-03

Shared Compensation Cap Allows Excessive Liquidator Rewards For dwstETH

Round 1
Sep 8, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/Dependencies/Constants.sol:90; source-snapshot/contracts/src/TroveManager.sol:358
CATEGORY

OOS - Configuration

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

TroveManager pays liquidators 0.5% of the collateral assigned to the Stability Pool offset, subject to COLL_GAS_COMPENSATION_CAP. This cap places an absolute limit on the collateral paid as gas compensation per liquidation, preventing the reward from continuing to grow proportionally with position size.

The cap was increased from the original Liquity Bold limit of 2 collateral tokens to 1,000 to accommodate dUSDC. However, this shared constant also raises the dwstETH cap despite its much higher value per token.

For dwstETH, the cap only takes effect when the SP collateral portion reaches 200,000 dwstETH, providing little practical restriction on large-position payouts beyond the 0.5% rate.

For example, a liquidation assigning 1,000 dwstETH to the SP would pay 5 dwstETH instead of Liquity Bold’s maximum of 2 collateral tokens. The additional 3 dwstETH reduces collateral available to SP depositors and/or the remaining collateral claimable by the borrower.

RECOMMENDATION

Consider configuring a separate compensation cap for each branch, calibrated to each collateral’s value.

title: MCR Validation Omits Gas Compensation, Reducing SP Rewards For dJPY And dJGB
detail:
L-04

MCR Validation Omits Gas Compensation, Reducing SP Rewards For dJPY And dJGB

Round 1
Sep 9, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/AddressesRegistry.sol:244; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Dependencies/Constants.sol:73; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Dependencies/Constants.sol:81
CATEGORY

Validation

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

AddressesRegistry._requireFinalizedRiskParams checks that MCR covers 100% + liquidationPenaltySP when finalizing a branch’s risk parameters. However, TroveManager deducts liquidator collateral compensation before allocating collateral to the Stability Pool. This finalization gate therefore does not ensure sufficient collateral for the full configured SP premium near MCR.

This affects the dJPY and dJGB parameter sets, which specify a 105.30% MCR and a 5% SP penalty. These values pass the check, but a liquidation just below MCR leaves approximately 105.30% × 99.5% = 104.7735% of offset debt value for the SP after collateral compensation. Depositors consequently receive approximately a 4.7735% premium instead of 5%, even before further price deterioration.

Covering both payments requires an MCR of at least approximately 105.52764%. The other branch parameter sets exceed this threshold. dJPY and dJGB are currently documented as inert branches, so this concern applies if they are activated with these values.

RECOMMENDATION

Consider replacing the existing MCR-versus-SP-penalty check in AddressesRegistry._requireFinalizedRiskParams with the following. The replacement makes the old check redundant.

if (_mcr * (COLL_GAS_COMPENSATION_DIVISOR - 1) < (1e18 + _liquidationPenaltySP) * COLL_GAS_COMPENSATION_DIVISOR) revert MCRBelowSPPenalty();


Increase MCR_DJPY and MCR_DJGB from 105.30% to at least 105.53% to satisfy the revised check.

RESOLUTION

title: Morpho Emergency Recovery Can Incur A Penalty Without Recovering Funds
detail:
L-05

Morpho Emergency Recovery Can Incur A Penalty Without Recovering Funds

Round 1
Sep 9, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralVault.sol:709; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/MorphoV2Strategy.sol:351; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/MorphoV2Strategy.sol:295; source-snapshot/contracts/script/PrepareDFGovernanceHandover.s.sol:328
CATEGORY

OOS - MEV

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

When the Morpho Vault V2’s normal withdrawal route lacks liquidity but another adapter can release assets, recovery requires separate deallocation and withdrawal calls. CollateralVault.forceDeallocateMorphoV2 releases liquidity while charging a penalty against the Strategy’s Morpho shares. A subsequent emergencyWithdrawFromMorphoV2 or sendToVault call retrieves the funds.

Morpho’s forceDeallocate places the released assets in the vault’s shared idle balance, without reserving them for the Strategy. Another eligible shareholder can withdraw this liquidity before the Strategy’s recovery call, without paying the deallocation penalty.

forceDeallocateMorphoV2 requires WRITEOFF_ROLE, while recovery requires either the Strategy owner through emergencyWithdrawFromMorphoV2 or ALLOCATOR_ROLE through sendToVault. The governance handover script requires the Strategy owner to be the Guardian and enforces distinct Guardian, Allocator, and Writeoff addresses. Under this role separation, a single role holder cannot atomically batch deallocation and recovery on its own.

The recovery path provides no combined entry point that makes deallocation conditional on successful withdrawal. Consequently, the subsequent recovery can fail while the penalty share burn remains committed, leaving the Strategy with fewer shares without recovering the intended funds.

RECOMMENDATION

Consider adding a function that deallocates assets and withdraws them to CollateralVault in the same transaction, reverting if the minimum required recovery amount is not received.

title: Bridge Burns Increase Redemption Fees
detail:
L-06

Bridge Burns Increase Redemption Fees

Round 1
Sep 9, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralRegistry.sol:138; source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralRegistry.sol:212; source-snapshot/contracts/src/JpydfToken.sol:219
CATEGORY

OOS - Business logic errors

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

CollateralRegistry._getUpdatedBaseRateFromRedemption calculates the base-rate increment using the redeemed amount divided by JpydfToken.totalSupply(). In the original BOLD implementation, there is no bridge burn path that reduces this denominator while leaving the corresponding Trove debt outstanding.

JPYdf introduces bridgeBurn, which reduces total supply without repaying Trove debt. Bridging out from mainnet through a burn/mint bridge therefore reduces the redemption fee denominator while the corresponding debt remains outstanding.

Consequently, the same redemption produces a larger base-rate increment as more supply is bridged out. For example, bridging out 50% of total supply doubles the increment, assuming the fee cap does not bind. This increases redemption costs and can discourage redemptions that would otherwise help restore the peg.

The effect applies to burn/mint bridging after activation. The documented launch configuration has zero bridge minters, and lock/unlock bridging does not cause this denominator reduction.

RECOMMENDATION

Document this behavior and consider using lock/unlock bridging. If burn/mint bridging is retained, consider replacing totalSupply() in the redemption fee calculation with a function that calculates total outstanding debt across all branches, consistently accounting for accrued interest.

RESOLUTION

title: Sky harvest can return principal as yield
detail:
L-07

Sky harvest can return principal as yield

Round 1
Sep 9, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION

https://github.com/GuardianOrg/mirror-deltaforesight-jpydf-audit-01a06231/blob/d59437beed41da49ff53c6796d2e3a09337af046/source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/BaseStrategy.sol#L367-L383 https://github.com/GuardianOrg/mirror-deltaforesight-jpydf-audit-01a06231/blob/d59437beed41da49ff53c6796d2e3a09337af046/source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/SkyUsdcSUsdsStrategy.sol#L380-L389

CATEGORY

OOS - Business logic errors

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

In BaseStrategy, sendProfitToVault calculates available yield as the strategy’s estimated underlying value minus its recorded principal. It withdraws that amount and forwards the entire actual return to the Vault, deliberately leaving _principal unchanged.

        uint256 withdrawnUnderlying = _doWithdraw(realizedProfit);
        if (withdrawnUnderlying == 0) {
            emit ProfitSentToVault(msg.sender, realizedProfit, 0);
            return 0;
        }

        // Yield-only push: `_principal` is intentionally left unchanged. Send
        // directly to the Vault buffer so Strategy valuation cache is not
        // reduced as if principal had been returned.
        sent = _sendUnderlyingYieldToVault(withdrawnUnderlying);


However, SkyUsdcSUsdsStrategy._doWithdraw can return more than requested. When converting the equivalent USDS amount would produce insufficient USDC, _usdsTargetForUsdc increases the input budget using maxConversionLossBps. The converter then purchases the maximum USDC supported by this inflated budget at the actual conversion fee, without limiting output to the requested withdrawal amount.

If the actual conversion fee is positive and lower than the configured allowance, the returned amount can exceed the available yield. The excess comes from principal and is transferred to the Vault, but _principal remains unchanged. The strategy therefore records more principal than it actually holds.

Future earnings must cover this accounting gap before becoming harvestable through sendProfitToVault. Even after all remaining assets are withdrawn, the strategy can retain nonzero recorded principal, blocking its removal until that residual principal is cleared.

RECOMMENDATION

Ensure Sky converts only enough USDS to obtain the requested USDC amount, and prevent yield-only transfers from exceeding the calculated yield.

title: Nonzero Strategy valuation failure pauses a fully backed branch
detail:
L-08

Nonzero Strategy valuation failure pauses a fully backed branch

Round 1
Sep 14, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
packages/jpydf-audit/source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralVault.sol:_totalUnderlyingWithAvailability():L834-L843
CATEGORY

OOS - denial-of-service

POC
https://github.com/GuardianOrg/SentryRepo-JPYdf---Round-1-01a0662feb047c87b2c30cb103f87c38/blob/refinery/poc-01a08010-597f-7ec7-9d3f-de3675737245/test/refinery-poc/nonzero-strategy-valuation-failure-pauses-a-fully-backed-bra-ab4fe92c.sol
REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

CollateralVault propagates any registered Strategy valuation failure as global backing unavailability before checking whether already-known raw assets independently cover all liabilities. This remains true for a live Strategy with nonzero tracked principal. DF price feeds convert the unavailable backing result into source failure, and PriceFeedProxy latches the recoverable oracle pause.

Impact: After the bounded valuation cache expires, failure of a live Strategy's read-only valuation endpoints can pause borrowing, risk-increasing operations, and normal redemption even though raw Vault custody alone fully backs every dToken and queued claim. The pause persists until the dependency or privileged incident handling restores valid oracle paths.

RECOMMENDATION

In backingRatioForPricing, return (1e18,true) as soon as accumulated known lower-bound assets cover liabilities. Propagate unavailable Strategy valuation only when the unknown contribution is needed to establish the backing ratio.

title: Zapper-only manager cannot perform Core's incident-safe close
detail:
L-09

Zapper-only manager cannot perform Core's incident-safe close

Round 1
Sep 14, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
packages/jpydf-audit/source-snapshot/contracts/src/Zappers/CollateralYieldZapper.sol:_openTroveWithDTokenCollateral():L523-L564
CATEGORY

logic / denial of service

POC
https://github.com/GuardianOrg/SentryRepo-JPYdf---Round-1-01a0662feb047c87b2c30cb103f87c38/blob/refinery/poc-01a08010-597f-7ec7-9d3f-de3675737245/test/refinery-poc/zapper-only-manager-cannot-perform-core-s-incident-safe-clos-cc869457.sol
REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

CollateralYieldZapper opens Core Troves with the zapper itself as the Core remove manager and receiver, then stores the user’s chosen remove manager only in the zapper’s local manager mapping. As a result, the configured manager can call zapper close flows, but cannot call BorrowerOperations.closeTrove directly.

This matters during a Vault redemption incident. CollateralYieldZapper.closeTroveToUnderlying first closes the Trove in Core, then immediately redeems the returned dToken through CollateralVault.redeem. If that redemption reverts or is paused, the whole transaction rolls back and the Trove remains open. The owner can still bypass the zapper by calling Core directly and receiving dToken, but the configured manager cannot split the rescue into “close now, redeem later.”

If the owner is unavailable, a funded emergency manager may be unable to close a risky Trove during a Vault incident. The position can then be liquidated even though Core’s dToken-returning close path would have allowed a safe exit.

RECOMMENDATION

Add an incident-safe zapper close path that lets the zapper-level remove manager close the Trove and forward dToken plus gas compensation to the configured receiver when Underlying redemption is unavailable.

title: Stale Zero Strategy Cache Can Misprice a Solvent Branch During Sky Preview Outage
detail:
L-10

Stale Zero Strategy Cache Can Misprice a Solvent Branch During Sky Preview Outage

Round 1
Sep 14, 2026
SEVERITY
LOW
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
packages/jpydf-audit/source-snapshot/contracts/src/CollateralVault.sol:receiveFromStrategy():L404-L423
CATEGORY

oracle accounting

POC
https://github.com/GuardianOrg/SentryRepo-JPYdf---Round-1-01a0662feb047c87b2c30cb103f87c38/blob/refinery/poc-01a08010-597f-7ec7-9d3f-de3675737245/test/refinery-poc/fresh-zero-strategy-cache-enables-near-free-drain-of-healthy-5d683b42.sol
REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

CollateralVault.receiveFromStrategy reduces a Strategy valuation cache when Underlying is returned to the Vault. If the returned amount is greater than or equal to the cached value, the cache is set to zero but remains initialized with its existing timestamp.

This can misprice a Strategy after a narrow Sky converter sequence. First, the Sky USDS to USDC converter must quote a low recoverable value, and that low Strategy value must be cached. Then the converter must recover to normal pricing before the allocator recalls more than the stale cached value, while assets still remain deployed in the Strategy. If the recalled buffer is redeemed and the Sky preview path later reverts before the cache expires, the Vault cannot refresh to the recovered live value and instead treats the zero cache as available.

At that point, the price feed reports a severe backing haircut instead of unavailable pricing, even though the Strategy may still hold recoverable assets. Borrowing, liquidation, redemption, and branch shutdown logic can then use the false price. The attack path depends on external Sky converter state changes and allocator timing, so likelihood is extremley low, but the stale zero cache can still create incorrect oracle driven outcomes while it remains fresh.

RECOMMENDATION

Refresh the Strategy valuation after a return and before reducing the cache when possible. If the refresh fails, invalidate the cache whenever the returned amount exhausts or exceeds the cached value, so an arithmetic zero is not treated as a live available zero.

RESOLUTION

detail:
I-01

Oracle pause blocks management fee reductions

Round 1
Sep 6, 2026

LOCATION

https://github.com/GuardianOrg/mirror-deltaforesight-jpydf-audit-01a06231/blob/d59437beed41da49ff53c6796d2e3a09337af046/source-snapshot/contracts/src/BorrowerOperations.sol#L894-L896

Business logic errors

DESCRIPTION

In BorrowerOperations, lowerBatchManagementFee invokes _requireIsNotShutDown, which rejects calls during both permanent shutdown and a recoverable oracle pause.

The new implementation preserves accrual but blocks the fee reductions. shutdownFromOracleFailure only sets isOracleFailureShutdown, leaving TroveManager.shutdownTime and the ActivePool shutdown state unchanged. As a result, borrowers continue accruing management fees that their batch manager may wish to reduce or waive until the branch is resumed.

Consider allowing management fee reductions during recoverable oracle pauses.

title: Truncation docs overstate redeemable amount
detail:
I-03

Truncation docs overstate redeemable amount

Round 1
Sep 7, 2026
SEVERITY
INFO
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION

https://github.com/GuardianOrg/mirror-deltaforesight-jpydf-audit-01a06231/blob/d59437beed41da49ff53c6796d2e3a09337af046/source-snapshot/contracts/src/RedemptionHelper.sol#L130-L142

CATEGORY

Documentation

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

The specification describes truncateRedemption as returning the maximum JPYdf amount that can be fully redeemed within the given iteration limit. However, the updated handling of unavailable redemption prices allows truncatedJpydf to exceed the expected amount actually redeemed.

When a branch passes the initial eligibility checks but its redemption price is unavailable, simulateRedemption keeps its allocation weight in totalProportions while excluding it from the simulated redemption. Consequently, available branches receive only their original proportional shares, and the unavailable branch’s share remains unfilled.

For example, a request for 100 JPYdf is split equally between two branches. If one branch’s redemption price is unavailable, the other can redeem only its 50 JPYdf share. Nevertheless, the helper calculates:

if (branch[i].redeemable && branch[i].proportion > 0) {
    // Extrapolate how much the entire redeemed JPYDF would
    // have been if this branch was redeemed proportionally.
    uint256 extrapolatedJpydf = branch[i].redeemedJpydf * totalProportions / branch[i].proportion;


This produces 50 * 2,000 / 1,000 = 100, so truncatedJpydf remains 100 even though the detailed quote estimates that only 50 JPYdf will be redeemed.

The partial allocation is intentional, and the detailed quotes correctly reflect the expected redemption. However, the documented guarantee of full redemption is inaccurate.

Integrators relying on the documentation may display truncatedJpydf as the expected amount redeemed, even when part of it will remain unspent.

RECOMMENDATION

Update the specification and interface comments to clarify that truncatedJpydf is the request amount associated with the quote and may be partially filled when branches are unavailable.

detail:
I-05

Incorrect NatSpec For Strategy Emergency Withdrawal Functions

Round 1
Sep 8, 2026
SEVERITY
INFO
CLIENT STATUS
Pending
LOCATION
source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/AaveV3Strategy.sol:291-292; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/ERC4626Strategy.sol:145-146; source-snapshot/contracts/src/Strategies/MorphoV2Strategy.sol:290-291
CATEGORY

OOS - Documentation

POC

No proof of concept linked

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

The emergency withdrawal comments in AaveV3Strategy.sol:291, ERC4626Strategy.sol:145, and MorphoV2Strategy.sol:290 direct GOV to call CollateralVault.writeoffStrategyPrincipal for residual losses.

However, this function requires WRITEOFF_ROLE, which is separate from GOV_ROLE. If these roles are assigned to different accounts, following the documented instructions results in a reverted call and could delay loss recognition during incident response.

RECOMMENDATION

Update all three comments to specify that an account holding the vault’s WRITEOFF_ROLE must call writeoffStrategyPrincipal.

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

ERC4626Strategy computes withdrawal assets with floor-rounded convertToAssets but invokes ERC4626 withdraw, whose standard ceiling conversion can burn an entire tracked share for a one-unit request. In a donation-inflated public venue, an honest allocator harvest/recall therefore transfers the strategy's principal-bearing share value to an external shareholder while only the requested dust reaches the Vault.

Impact: A permissionless shareholder can donate to inflate exchange rate, then redeem the surviving share after an expected allocator call, recovering the donation plus roughly the protocol principal. The strategy is left at zero NAV against unchanged principal, creating a real backing deficit and potentially blocking solvency-gated Vault operations.

RECOMMENDATION

Document this as an ERC4626 venue selection requirement. Approved vaults should have donation inflation protection or otherwise bounded share rounding behavior, and operators should monitor exchange rate inflation so sendToVault is not called with dust asset amounts when one share is worth significant principal.

POC

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

VaultV2 calculates performance fees on positive growth from the previously recorded _totalAssets, without a historical high-water mark. After a recorded loss lowers that baseline, subsequent recovery can incur fees even before assets exceed their pre-loss value. This requires a nonzero performance fee when recovery is recognized. Fee activation settles existing accrual under the old rate, so it does not retroactively charge recovery already recognized. If performance fees are enabled, recovery can mint fee shares and dilute MorphoV2Strategy’s holdings despite no net gain over the pre-loss value. This mechanism causes no performance-fee dilution while performanceFee == 0.

RECOMMENDATION

Check the vault’s fees before allocating funds, monitor proposed fee changes, and withdraw before an unacceptable change takes effect.

REMEDIATION

Link the fix

DESCRIPTION

The collateral policy states that both liquidation penalties must be payable from collateral at MCR. However, the authoritative Parameter Catalog and finalization checks require this only for the Stability Pool penalty. The authorized finalizer can therefore approve MCR=105%, SP penalty=5%, and redistribution penalty=20%, assuming the remaining checks pass. This satisfies the implemented rules but conflicts with the broader policy.

Consequently, a future branch could receive permanent parameters that cannot support the full configured redistribution penalty near MCR. Liquidation remains capped at available collateral, and current Day-1 parameters satisfy both bounds.

RECOMMENDATION

Clarify whether MCR must cover both liquidation penalties, and if so, enforce this during finalization and deployment.
